title: Check feedback for the answer reworded
statement: Check wrong-option feedback for the right answer said in other words, which a word-match check misses and a truth check never asks about.
example: The code check fires only on a run of at least three of the right option's own words, so a shipped quick check whose wrong-option feedback gave the answer in other words passed it.
detail: The shared code check flags a wrong option's feedback only when it repeats a run of the right option's words as long as the option, with a floor of three words, so it cannot catch a key of one or two words or any key said in other words. A quick check on a poem shipped ready with two wrong-option feedback lines that gave the keyed answer in other words, one telling the reader who the poem's speaker is, although its prompt says such feedback must not name the right answer and its judge asks nothing about feedback. In a remade film check, two such lines were judged only on whether they were true (0.72, 0.95), while a later draft that repeated the option's own words was caught.
against: Whether a line names the answer in other words is itself a judgment, so a paraphrase check would need person-labelled cases before it holds a block. Pointing back to what was said is what the prompt asks for, so the line may count as a hint rather than a give-away: "wrong option's sends the viewer back to what was said without using the right option's words" (`g9/transformer/src/mechanics/video-essay.js`, line 54).
